extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, IP offices, patent statisticians, researchers, and analysts using WIPO patent statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, methodological notes and data‑handling rules used by WIPO in compiling and presenting global patent statistics (e.g., origin determination, patent families, technology mapping, pendency categories, and interpretation caveats).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of origin of a patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of a patent application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent filing activity by origin includes resident applications and applications filed abroad. Applications filed at regional offices are considered equivalent to multiple applications in the relevant member states. (See the glossary for the definition of equivalent application.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application / equivalent grant (reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO refers readers to the glossary for the definition of 'equivalent application' and 'equivalent grant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional office filings are treated as equivalent to multiple national applications in relevant member states when preparing origin-based indicators; equivalent grants are defined similarly (see glossary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent families are defined as patent applications interlinked by one or more of the following: priority claim, Patent Cooperation Treaty national phase entry, continuation, continuation‑in‑part, internal priority, and addition or division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent families here include only those families associated with patent applications for inventions and exclude those associated with utility model applications. Patent family indicators are used to take account of applicants filing in multiple jurisdictions (to avoid simple double counting). Sources: WIPO Statistics Database and EPO PATSTAT database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign‑oriented patent family
rubrics_metrics.description: A special subset of patent families comprises foreign‑oriented patent families: those that have at least one filing office different from the office of the applicant’s country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some foreign‑oriented patent families include only one filing office because applicants may choose to file directly with a foreign office (example: a Canadian applicant filing directly with the USPTO without a previous Canadian filing — that application and any subsequent related filings with the USPTO form a foreign‑oriented patent family).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping IPC to fields of technology (IPC technology concordance)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO’s International Patent Classification (IPC) technology concordance table is used to convert IPC symbols into 35 corresponding fields of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correspondence between IPC symbols and technology fields is not always apparent (there is no one‑to‑one correspondence). It is therefore difficult to capture all patents in a specific technology field, but IPC‑based definitions are likely to capture the vast majority. (Electronic version of the concordance: www.wipo.int/ipstats.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Published patent applications: publication lag
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to published patent applications and there is a minimum delay of 18 months between the application date and the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the publication delay, year‑by‑year published application counts reflect applications filed at least 18 months earlier; interpret time series accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of absolute counts vs equivalent counts for origin data
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin data in some tables are based on absolute counts, not equivalent counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting flows of non‑resident applications and some top‑office/origin tables, note whether counts are absolute (raw filings) or equivalent (adjusted for regional office filings) as this affects comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caveat for 'share of applications granted' metric
rubrics_metrics.description: The share of applications granted should not be interpreted as grant rates, as they are based on the examination date rather than the date when the application was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of grants in a given year relates to applications filed in previous years. WIPO collects data using a common questionnaire and methodology, but due to differences in patent procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized — exercise caution when making cross‑office comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending applications: category separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending application data are separated between (a) all patent applications, at any stage in the process, that are awaiting a final decision by a patent office (including those for which applicants have not filed a request for examination, where applicable), and (b) patent applications undergoing examination for which the applicant has requested examination (where such separate requests are necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application processing varies between offices (some auto‑proceed to examination unless withdrawn; others require a separate request). The split is provided to take procedural differences across offices into account when measuring pending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of patents in force (calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The average age of patents in force is calculated using the formula Σ(p*y)/Σp, where p is the number of patents in force and y the number of years between filing and reporting year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This weighted‑average formula is used to produce the average age figures shown for offices (e.g., comparisons between 2016 and 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents in force as percentage of total applications (calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentages are calculated as the number of patent applications filed in year t and in force in 2020, divided by the total number of patent applications filed in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This measure shows the distribution of patents in force in 2021 as a percentage of total applications in the year of filing. Note that maintenance fee choices and lapse decisions affect these percentages; not all offices provide the necessary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor gender attribution methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: To attribute gender to inventors’ names recorded in PCT applications, WIPO produced a world gender–name dictionary based on information from 13 different public sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender is attributed to a given name on a country‑by‑country basis because certain names may be considered male in one country but female in another. Users should be aware of possible misattribution and cultural/name ambiguities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for top offices / top origins displayed
rubrics_metrics.description: Top offices and origins shown in tables/figures are selected based on data availability and specific inclusion criteria stated for each table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The top 20 offices and origins are selected based on available 2021 data, broken down by country of origin.' For resident applications per USD 100 billion GDP (A35), top 20 origins were included if they had GDP > USD 25 billion (2017 PPP) and >100 resident patent applications. For resident applications per million population (A36), top 20 origins were included if population >5 million and >100 resident patent applications. Space constraints may further limit presentation.
